methodological_rigor.justification: This is a large international phase III noninferiority RCT (n=6,088) with pre-specified noninferiority margin (HR 1.13) carried over from the original report, 1:1 randomization with minimization on key prognostic factors (regimen, sex, site, T stage, N stage), and extended follow-up (median 113 months per abstract, 75 months per Results — a minor internal discrepancy). The analysis uses multivariable Cox models with verification of the proportional hazards assumption via scaled Schoenfeld residuals and switches to restricted mean survival time when PH is violated (as noted for rectal cancer). Limitations include that OS is a secondary endpoint (DFS was primary), regimen was chosen by the clinician rather than randomized (so CAPOX vs FOLFOX comparisons are non-randomized and confounded by indication), and multiplicity across the numerous subgroup/regimen noninferiority tests is not explicitly addressed. Toxicity and QoL were not updated at this follow-up, so trade-off claims rest on the original report.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a single large individual randomized controlled trial of adjuvant chemotherapy duration in CRC, mapping to Oxford LoE 1b. Clinical relevance is very high: the primary outcome (OS) is patient-relevant, the trial directly addresses a long-standing standard-of-care question (3 vs 6 months of oxaliplatin-based adjuvant chemo), and findings — noninferiority of 3 months overall and for CAPOX, with substantial reduction in cumulative neuropathy — are practice-informing and align with/extend the IDEA collaboration guidance. The rectal cancer subgroup is unique within IDEA and directly relevant to current total neoadjuvant therapy practice.

reporting_quality.justification: CONSORT applies as this is a phase III RCT; the manuscript references the original full report and protocol for complete methods and includes a CONSORT flow diagram (Fig 1), pre-specified noninferiority margin, trial registration (ISRCTN59757862), ethics approval, and informed consent. Key items such as randomization/minimization, endpoint definitions, PH checking, and subgroup analyses are reported, though adverse events are deferred entirely to the prior publication and some reporting is terse because this is a follow-up update. There is no explicit data/code availability statement in the text provided; sharing posture is weak based on what is visible.

novelty_literature.justification: The novelty is empirical and incremental: extended-follow-up OS results from a previously reported large RCT within the IDEA collaboration. The main new contributions are (i) confirmation of OS noninferiority for 3 months overall in SCOT (not previously demonstrated for an individual IDEA trial), (ii) regimen-specific findings (CAPOX noninferior; FOLFOX not), and (iii) unique rectal cancer subgroup data. These findings refine but do not overturn the IDEA pooled analysis conclusions, so this is a meaningful extension rather than a paradigm shift.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized, concise, and appropriate for a mature-follow-up report; the abstract is quantitatively grounded and the Introduction effectively situates SCOT within IDEA. Results are reported with HRs, 95% CIs, and noninferiority P-values, and the Discussion appropriately contextualizes regimen-dependent findings and the NNT framing for high-risk stage III. One notable inconsistency: the abstract reports median follow-up of 113 months while Results states 75 months (IQR 61–91), which editors should resolve. Figure/table captions are informative and standalone-interpretable.

key_strengths: Large international phase III RCT (n=6,088) with pre-specified noninferiority margin and long-term OS follow-up
Rigorous survival analysis with PH verification via Schoenfeld residuals and RMST fallback where PH violated
Practice-informing finding: OS noninferiority for 3 months overall and for CAPOX, with major reduction in cumulative neuropathy
Unique rectal cancer subgroup within the IDEA collaboration, directly relevant to current TNT practice
Clear CONSORT flow diagram, trial registration, ethics approval, and transparent reference to the original protocol
key_concerns: Internal inconsistency in reported median follow-up (abstract 113 months vs Results 75 months, IQR 61–91)
OS is a secondary endpoint and multiplicity across many subgroup/regimen noninferiority tests is not explicitly addressed
Regimen (CAPOX vs FOLFOX) was clinician-chosen rather than randomized, so regimen-specific comparisons are susceptible to confounding by indication
Toxicity and quality-of-life data were not updated for this long-term analysis despite being central to the risk-benefit framing
No explicit data or code availability statement visible in the manuscript
chief_reviewer.rationale: Content-wise this is a definitive long-term OS update of a landmark phase III noninferiority trial with directly practice-informing conclusions, warranting consideration at tier 1 oncology journals pending resolution of the follow-up discrepancy and clarification of multiplicity and data-sharing posture.
